purpose: The 2026-10-08 G1/G2 plan's rows WP-1A-A0-003 ("actor, scope และ correlation ต่อกันได้จาก request ถึง DB ไม่มี raw error รั่ว และ cross-tenant request ต้องถูกปฏิเสธ") and WP-1A-A0-004 ("ผ่านเทสต์ crash/restart, duplicate, timeout และ replay ไม่มี event หายที่ขอบ transaction") are each met end to end only by code that reaches the database. Both packages wrote their provider-free part and moved the rest out: WP-1A-A0-003 moved its provider-bound increment and acceptance_criteria[7] to "the future package proposed as WP-1A-A0-006" on 2026-10-18 (its open_blockers[25]); WP-1A-A0-004 excludes the database part (scope.exclude[0]) and says so in acceptance_criteria[6]. This package holds both: the Postgres job store and outbox store under RFC-2026-028's app_worker_login (RFC-2026-029 §2.7/3, `pg` in src/modules/platform-kernel/adapters/** only), the worker's dispatcher route and composition root in apps/worker (§2.8, §6.1), and the request path's Supabase session, per-request client under the user's JWT and real tenant access directory (§2.7/1, §8/7). It is reversible work under RFC-2026-029 §7 and RFC-2026-034 §2.1: synthetic data, the local and CI Postgres container only, no provider account and no credential bound. Its first pull request only opens the package; the decisions each later increment needs are in open_blockers.

No source code.

src/modules/platform-kernel/adapters/: the Postgres implementations of WP-1A-A0-004's JobStorePort and of its OutboxPort, PublisherPort target and ConsumerLedgerPort, over app.jobs, app.outbox_events and app.consumer_ledger (050, 174), through `pg` as app_worker_login. Every transaction opens `begin; set local role app_worker;` and, for a carried statement, sets app.workspace_id with set_config(..., true) from the job's or event's tenant context (RFC-2026-028 §3.1); never SET or SET ROLE without LOCAL, never RESET ROLE inside an open transaction. The claim goes through the broker RFC-2026-022 §5/6 names once its migration exists (open_blockers). The adapters enforce WP-1A-A0-004's D6 caps before any row is written (A1-303-I2; required_human_authorities[1]) and read each caller-supplied object once (A1-302-I9, A1-303-I3). The runner carries RFC-2026-028's A1R-2 checks, which RFC-2026-029 §2.7/3 (lines 132-134) requires of the dispatcher (RFC-2026-028 line 6, A1R-2 and A1-173-1; §5/13, lines 367-375): (a) at connect and before `set local role` in every job transaction, it reads current_user, session_user and the role's pg_db_role_setting rows and refuses unless current_user = session_user = 'app_worker_login' and no pg_db_role_setting row exists for the role (the production copy of scripts/db/authz-proofs.mjs's workerSessionStartProblem); (b) at the start of every job transaction, after `set local role app_worker` and before its own set_config(..., true), it refuses when current_setting('app.workspace_id', true) is neither null nor empty. index.ts does not re-export them (RFC-2026-029 §6.3/5).

apps/worker/: the dispatcher route handler and nothing else in app/, and the composition root in composition/ that reads the worker credential and wires the job store (RFC-2026-029 §2.7/3, §2.8, §6.1, §8/5). The route authenticates the caller by a dedicated secret compared in constant time, refuses every call when the secret is unset or empty, refuses on a Preview deployment, and stops within a per-round time budget below the function's maximum duration (D6). Not deployed and not provisioned.

apps/web/composition/: the request path's provider wiring (A0's recommendation, open_blockers): the Supabase client created per request with the project's public key and the user's session from cookies (@supabase/ssr), the session cookies HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax (RFC-2026-029 §2.7/1, §8/7), and the real tenant access directory and principal adapters behind WP-1A-A0-003's ports. Every directory read is an RFC-2026-021 allowlist entry or a database function reviewed with A1; none exists today. No apps/web file outside composition/ is written.

acceptance_criteria: OPENING PR: the branch resolves to WP-1A-A0-006 alone; BRANCH_OWNERSHIP gains exactly one row and test-kits/integrity-manifest.json changes only that file's digest; validate-work-packages, validate-work-package-ownership and validate-work-package-role-separation exit 0; npm run check is green; no source file changes.

Job store adapter, on the local and CI Postgres container against app.jobs: it passes the behaviour WP-1A-A0-004 pins on its in-memory fake (enqueue with an existing dedupe_key in the same workspace returns the existing job and writes no row; two claimers at once get at most one lease; a crash mid-run is reclaimed after lease expiry by another worker; a restart with a new pool resumes; a duplicate enqueue and a duplicate delivery have no second effect; a handler exceeding its timeout is recorded and released). A statement issued before SET LOCAL ROLE fails with 42501; no session-level SET ROLE, SET or RESET ROLE is issued. A1R-2 (RFC-2026-029 §2.7/3, lines 132-134; RFC-2026-028 line 6), through the production runner's code path, not a harness copy: (a) session check — a bare app_worker_login session starts its job; negative controls: a session whose current_user or session_user is not app_worker_login (for example a superuser session, or one under `set session authorization`) is refused before any job statement, and a session after `alter role app_worker_login set role = 'app_worker'` (one pg_db_role_setting row) is refused at connect and at the next job transaction's start, and a runner with the check removed goes red on both; (b) §5/13 (RFC-2026-028 lines 367-375) — two consecutive jobs on one connection, the first setting app.workspace_id with set_config(..., true): the second starts clean; negative control: the first sets it with set_config(..., false), the second refuses to start, and a runner without the check goes red.

The adapters enforce WP-1A-A0-004's D6 caps (max_attempts 20, timeout_seconds 900 while required_human_authorities[1] holds): an enqueue above either writes no row and rejects with the stable error the fake uses; each caller-supplied object is read once.

Outbox store adapter, on the container against app.outbox_events and app.consumer_ledger: an event appended in the producing transaction is committed with it or not at all (a rollback after the append leaves no outbox row; a commit leaves exactly one), so no event is lost or invented at the transaction boundary; the relay marks dispatched_at only after the publish resolved and stops at the first entry it cannot publish or mark; a consumer records (workspace_id, consumer, event_id) in the transaction that makes its effect visible, so a replay, a duplicate, or a redelivery after a relay crash between publish and mark has no second effect; the relayed envelope carries the full CTR-TEN-001 tenant_context (A1-302-I2).

Tenant isolation, on the container, once the forward migration is in place: as app_worker under workspace A's GUC no row of workspace B in any of the three tables is read, updated or inserted; a claim through the broker returns the claimed job's workspace and runs the job's carried statements under it; authenticated and anon read and write nothing; each case has a negative control that fails it (the policy or the broker's owner policy dropped).

Dispatcher route in apps/worker, on fakes: a missing, wrong or empty secret is refused, with the comparison constant-time; an unset secret refuses every call; a Preview deployment refuses; a round stops within its time budget under a fake clock; apps/worker/app/ serves that route and nothing else; outside apps/worker/composition/** no file reads the worker credential, and nothing under apps/web reaches pg or src/modules/platform-kernel/adapters/** (node scripts/verify-app-boundaries.mjs --require-parser).

Request path in apps/web/composition, on fakes: the session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax (RFC-2026-029 §8/7), shown by a test on the code that sets them; the Supabase client is created per request with the public key and the user's session, never the service-role key (§8/5); the tenant access directory admits only what an RFC-2026-021 entry or a reviewed database function admits; a cross-tenant or unknown scope is refused with WP-1A-A0-003's uniform error.

MOVED IN from WP-1A-A0-003 acceptance_criteria[7] and WP-1A-A0-004 acceptance_criteria[6]: actor, scope and correlation chain from the request to the database with no raw error leaked and a cross-tenant request refused, and a durable worker over app.jobs with a transactional outbox on the database. On the CI container these are met by the criteria above; on a hosted Supabase project they are met only after provisioning (WP-1A-A6-001, WP-1A-A1-001) and RFC-2026-034 §2.1's later decision, in WP-1A-A0-005's slice, which this package does not contain.

No job or event record, error, failure report or log line carries a thrown value's or a driver error's message, name, stack, SQL text or connection string; database failures map to CTR-ERR-001 stable errors; npm run typecheck and npm run test:app pass.
